newsitem.title: USA: Knape & Vogt sees higher FY 97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Knape & Vogt sees higher FY 97 sales.

text.p: Knape & Vogt Manufacturing Co said Thursday it expects an eight percent growth in fiscal 1997 sales over a year ago.

Sales for all of fiscal 1996 were $163.0 million. In a statement, President and Chief Executive Officer Al Perry said he also expects the positive trends of the first nine months of fiscal 1997 to continue.
"This year, we have been implementing significant changes based on our June 1996, restructuring plan, and we have been working to sell assets that no longer fit with our core businesses," he said.

The maker of storage-related products reported income from continuing operations of $2.06 million, up from $2.04 million in the third period ended March 31. The 1997 results include a $246,235 charge relating to the sale of of its Modar Inc unit, also announced Thursday.
For the nine-month period, the firm reported income from continuing operations of $6.2 million, versus $4.6 million a year ago. Sales were $132.7 million, up from $122.7 million.
